edges.description: The expanded repeat is translated in frame, giving a ZFHX3 protein that carries a long polyglycine domain and accumulates in patient cells.
Knocking down ZFHX3 in patient cells normalizes the mTOR and autophagy markers, so the autophagy change depends on the mutant protein.
Neuronal ZFHX3 accumulation is presumed to drive cerebellar degeneration; the intervening steps have not been studied in neurons.

nodes.description: Neuronal loss is widespread in the brainstem: pontine, vestibular, oculomotor-related (abducens, prepositus hypoglossi, raphe interpositus), auditory, trigeminal, facial, dorsal vagal and hypoglossal nuclei, the inferior olive and the substantia nigra. nodes.description: Steady-state ZFHX3 protein is increased in patient fibroblasts and iPSCs, and patient iPSCs contain large cytoplasmic polyglycine aggregates that co-label with ubiquitin. In autopsy tissue, neurons carry p62- and ubiquitin-positive intranuclear (and in one Swedish case also intracytoplasmic) inclusions in the pons, medulla and elsewhere in the brain, and in myenteric plexus neurons. The inclusions do not react with the polyglutamine antibody 1C2. Whether aggregation, the excess protein or a nuclear loss of function drives neuronal death is not established.

nodes.description: Dermal fibroblasts from four affected members of the Utah kindred and iPSCs derived from one of them. Patient iPSCs became apoptotic when induced to differentiate into neurons, so neuronal cells could not be studied. The system mixes primary fibroblasts with undifferentiated iPSCs. The polyglycine aggregates were seen only in the iPSCs, not the fibroblasts. Raised mTOR, phospho-mTOR and p62, and their normalization by ZFHX3 knockdown, were shown in both cell types; LC3-II was measured in iPSCs.

A prominent axonal sensory neuropathy is present in essentially all patients and was the defining feature of the original kindred. At autopsy the posterior columns and the dorsal column nuclei degenerate, which with the reduced sensory nerve responses points to loss of primary sensory neurons. Proprioceptive loss adds a sensory component to the ataxia.

meta.association: Heterozygous pure GGC repeat expansion in exon 10 of ZFHX3. Loss-of-function ZFHX3 variants cause a different, neurodevelopmental disorder, and SCA4 patients have no neurodevelopmental or dysmorphic features. Screening of large ataxia cohorts outside populations of Swedish descent has found few or no carriers.

nodes.description: A heterozygous GGC repeat expansion in exon 10 of ZFHX3. Normal alleles carry about 21 units interrupted by GGT and AGT codons; expanded alleles (roughly 40 to 57 units in reported families) are pure GGC. The expansion is in frame and encodes an elongated polyglycine tract in the C-terminal part of a roughly 400 kDa homeodomain-zinc finger transcription factor. It is not detectable by short-read exome sequencing.

evidence.snippet: we found a heterozygous (GGC)n repeat expansion in the last coding exon of the zinc finger homeobox 3 (ZFHX3) gene that segregates with disease, ranging between 48 and 57 GGC repeats in affected probands.

evidence.snippet: Using phased sequencing results from individuals from Utah, Iowa, and Southern Sweden, we confirmed a common ~2000-year-old ancestral haplotype harbouring the repeat expansion.

genetic_context.description: Germline and inherited from an affected parent; every reported allele descends from one Swedish founder. Whether the expanded protein acts through a toxic or a normal-function gain is unresolved, so no functional impact category is recorded.
